title: Open algebraic-space morphisms lift generalizations through a specified point
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact point space. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between quasi-separated algebraic spaces whose point map is open. For every $x_0\in|X|$ and $y_1\in|Y|$ with $f(x_0)\in\overline{\{y_1\}}$, there is $x_1\in|X|$ such that $x_0\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$ and $f(x_1)=y_1$. Neither surjectivity nor local finite presentation is assumed.

source.place: Rydh section 1, paragraph preceding Remark (1.3), printed p.5, and Remark (2.5)(2), printed p.8; algebraic-space extensions Remark (1.8) and end of section 2, printed p.11. proof.text: Choose an affine component $U$ of an etale presentation $p:U\to X$ and $u_0\in U$ with $p(u_0)=x_0$, using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. The point map of $p$ is open and continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus $h=f\circ p:U\to Y$ is open: $h(V)=f(p(V))$ is open for every open $V\subseteq U$. The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and hence its point space is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral].

Choose a field representative $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ of $y_1$ by [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Its source has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $Y$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] makes $a$ quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-constructible-closed] to the whole (closed) constructible point space of $\operatorname{Spec}K$: its image $\{y_1\}$ is constructible-topology closed in $Y$. Both $U$ and $Y$ are quasi-separated, so [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison] makes $|h|$ continuous for these topologies. Therefore $F=h^{-1}\{y_1\}\subseteq U$ is closed in the constructible topology of the affine scheme $U$.

source.place: Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), (1); field representatives: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points). Agent argument using the cited constructible-topology nodes.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ be the quasi-compact open neighborhoods of $u_0$ in the spectral space $U$; they form a neighborhood basis by [def-weil-spectral-space]. Each $B\in\mathcal B$ is closed in the constructible topology by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. For any finite list $B_1,\ldots,B_r$ in $\mathcal B$, the open set $V=B_1\cap\cdots\cap B_r$ contains $u_0$ (take $V=U$ if $r=0$). Since $h(V)$ is an open neighborhood of $h(u_0)=f(x_0)$ and $f(x_0)\in\overline{\{y_1\}}$, it contains $y_1$. Thus $F\cap V$ is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact], $U$ is quasi-compact in its constructible topology. If $F\cap\bigcap_{B\in\mathcal B}B$ were empty, the constructible opens $U\setminus F$ and $U\setminus B$ would cover $U$. A finite subcover would contradict the preceding nonempty finite intersections. Choose $u_1$ in this intersection. Then $h(u_1)=y_1$, and every neighborhood of $u_0$ contains $u_1$, so $u_0\in\overline{\{u_1\}}$.

source.place: Tag 0901 (lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact), quasi-compactness; definition-constructible-topology immediately preceding it. Agent finite-subcover argument.

proof.text: Set $x_1=p(u_1)$. Then $f(x_1)=h(u_1)=y_1$. To verify specialization directly, let $O\subseteq|X|$ be any open neighborhood of $x_0$. By continuity of $p$ from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $p^{-1}O$ is a neighborhood of $u_0$, so it contains $u_1$. Hence $x_1\in O$, proving $x_0\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$. This proves the required lifting using only openness of $f$, with no surjectivity or finite-presentation assumption.
